key_insight: Sparse-QITE uses sparsity-promoting regularization to find much smaller QITE generators, dramatically reducing circuit depth and gate count while preserving ground-state accuracy.
engineering_relevance: By shrinking the active Pauli support and measurement burden, Sparse-QITE makes imaginary-time quantum simulation more practical for near-term hardware and larger problem sizes.
method: Regularize the QITE generator to encourage sparse Pauli coefficients.
Add adaptive regularization selection during evolution for better sparsity–accuracy balance.
Use an active-discovery variant to cut the number of Pauli expectation values that must be measured.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks on 1D transverse-field Ising and antiferromagnetic Heisenberg models show a controllable sparsity–accuracy trade-off, strong compression at high accuracy, and in some large-domain cases only about 1% of the standard-QITE gate count after transpilation.
watch_item: Sparsification can reduce resources, but the regularization strength must be tuned carefully to avoid degrading approximation quality or limiting performance outside the tested model families.
paper_title: Sparse-QITE: Discovering Compact Generators for Quantum Imaginary-Time Evolution via Regularization Methods
